explanation: In modern C++, smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr provide automatic and exception-safe memory management by owning a dynamically allocated object exclusively. When a std::unique_ptr goes out of scope, it automatically deletes the managed object, preventing memory leaks. It enforces unique ownership semantics, meaning only one unique_ptr can own a given resource at a time, which simplifies resource management and enhances code safety.
code_example: // Create a unique_ptr to manage a Widget instance
std::cout << "widgetPtr is now null after move" << std::endl;
// unique_ptr automatically deletes the Widget when it goes out of scope
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::unique_ptr to manage a dynamically allocated Widget object. It shows how to create a unique_ptr using std::make_unique, how ownership can be transferred via std::move, and how the resource is automatically cleaned up when the unique_ptr goes out of scope. This exemplifies modern C++'s RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom, ensuring safe and exception-resistant memory management.
